android.legacy-schema-unsupported.body:
This backup uses the database layout WhatsApp used before 2021, which this
version cannot read yet.

If the phone still works, making a fresh backup will produce the current
layout. Otherwise this is worth reporting: the older layout is documented
and supporting it is a matter of work rather than discovery.
android.legacy-schema-unsupported.title: This backup uses the layout WhatsApp used before 2021

android.not-a-message-database.body:
This is a database, but not the one that holds messages.

After decrypting you should have a file called msgstore.db. Two other files
sit beside it in a backup and are easy to confuse with it: wa.db holds
contacts, and chatsettingsbackup.db holds preferences.
android.not-a-message-database.title: That database is not the one with the messages in it

android.unreadable.body:
The file could not be opened at all. Check that the path is right, that the
file finished copying, and that you have permission to read it.
android.unreadable.title: That file could not be opened at all

backupfs.corrupt-manifest.body:
The backup's own index could not be read, which usually means the backup
did not finish.

Make a fresh one. A half-written backup cannot be repaired, and using one
would give an archive missing whatever had not been copied yet.
backupfs.corrupt-manifest.title: The backup's own index could not be read

backupfs.encrypted.body:
This backup is encrypted, so nothing but the phone it came from can read
it. That is Apple's design and not something any program can work around.

Turn encryption off and make a fresh backup:

  Finder > the phone in the sidebar > uncheck "Encrypt local backup"

It asks for the password that was set. Your chats are unaffected, but an
unencrypted backup leaves out saved passwords and Health data, so turn it
back on when you are done.

Make the safety copy first: Finder keeps one backup per device and
overwrites it. Right-click the existing backup in Manage Backups and choose
Archive, and it will survive.
backupfs.encrypted.title: That backup is encrypted

backupfs.file-not-found.body:
That file is not in this backup.

WhatsApp's message store is called ChatStorage.sqlite. If it is missing,
the phone may not have had WhatsApp installed when the backup was made, or
the backup may have finished early. Check the backup's date and make a
fresh one if it looks old.
backupfs.file-not-found.title: That file is not in this backup

backupfs.not-a-backup.body:
That folder is not an iPhone backup.

A backup folder is named after the device's identifier, a long string of
digits and letters, and holds Manifest.db, Manifest.plist, Info.plist and
Status.plist. The folder above it holds one such folder per device.

Run "amberkeep backups" to find them.
backupfs.not-a-backup.title: That folder is not an iPhone backup

backupfs.not-a-file.body:
That entry in the backup is a folder rather than a file, so there is
nothing to take out of it.
backupfs.not-a-file.title: That entry in the backup is a folder

backupfs.permission-denied.body:
macOS keeps iPhone backups behind Full Disk Access, and this program does
not have it.

  System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access

Add your terminal, or whichever program is running this, then run the
command again. Nothing is granted to anybody else by doing so, and it can
be taken away afterwards.

If you would rather not, copy the backup folder somewhere ordinary in
Finder and point at the copy instead:

  amberkeep extract --backup /path/to/the/copy --out .
backupfs.permission-denied.title: macOS will not let this program read your backups yet

backupfs.unreadable.body:
The backup could not be read. Check the path, and that the backup finished
copying if it came from somewhere else.
backupfs.unreadable.title: The backup could not be read

crypt15.crypt14-needs-root.body:
This is an older backup format, locked with a key WhatsApp keeps inside its
own private storage on the phone. Reaching it needs root access.

The straightforward path is to make a new backup instead: turn on
end-to-end encrypted backup with a 64-digit key, tap Back Up, and use the
msgstore.db.crypt15 file it produces.
crypt15.crypt14-needs-root.title: This is the older backup format, and it needs root

crypt15.key-format.body:
The key is the 64-digit one WhatsApp shows you, in eight groups of eight
characters. Spaces, dashes and line breaks in the file are fine.

If you only have a password, it cannot be used here: WhatsApp releases the
key to the app after checking the password and never lets it leave the
phone. Switch the backup to a 64-digit key and back up again. No chats are
lost by doing this.

  WhatsApp > Settings > Chats > Chat backup > End-to-end encrypted backup
crypt15.key-format.title: That is not a 64-digit key

crypt15.malformed-file.body:
This does not look like a WhatsApp backup.

The file you want is called msgstore.db.crypt15 and lives in
Android/media/com.whatsapp/WhatsApp/Databases on the phone. The files
beginning "msgstore-increment" are partial and cannot be read on their own.
crypt15.malformed-file.title: That file is not a WhatsApp backup

crypt15.passkey-not-supported.body:
This backup is locked with a passkey, which never leaves the phone, so no
program on a computer can open it.

Switch to a 64-digit key and make a fresh backup. Your chats are untouched
by the change.

  WhatsApp > Settings > Chats > Chat backup > End-to-end encrypted backup
crypt15.passkey-not-supported.title: This backup is locked with a passkey

crypt15.unexpected-plaintext.body:
The key was right and the file is intact, but its contents are in a shape
this version does not recognise. That usually means the backup came from a
newer WhatsApp release than this build knows about.

It is worth reporting, with the WhatsApp version that made the backup.
crypt15.unexpected-plaintext.title: This backup is in a shape this version does not know

crypt15.wrong-key.body:
Two things produce this, and they cannot be told apart from outside:

  * The key belongs to a different backup. Check you copied the key that
    WhatsApp showed for this phone and this account.
  * The file is incomplete. Copy it off the phone again and compare the
    size with the original before trying once more.
crypt15.wrong-key.title: That key does not open this backup

export.archive-exists.body:
An archive is already there, and it will not be overwritten by accident.

Choose an empty directory with --out, or pass --force to replace what is
there. Nothing else in the directory is touched either way.
export.archive-exists.title: There is already an archive there

ios.encrypted-backup.body:
This file is still encrypted, which is what an encrypted iPhone backup
holds instead of a database.

Turn backup encryption off in Finder, iTunes or the Apple Devices app and
make a fresh backup. Turning it off asks for the password that was set.

Your chats are not affected by the change, but Health and saved passwords
are left out of an unencrypted backup, so turn encryption back on
afterwards.
ios.encrypted-backup.title: That file is still encrypted

ios.not-a-message-store.body:
This is a database, but not the one an iPhone keeps messages in.

The file you want is called ChatStorage.sqlite. It lives inside an iPhone
backup, under the group container for WhatsApp, and comes with two files
beside it whose names end in -wal and -shm. All three are needed: the one
ending -wal holds whatever had not yet been written into the main file.
ios.not-a-message-store.title: That database is not the one an iPhone keeps messages in

ios.unreadable.body:
The iPhone message store could not be read. Check that the path is right,
that the file finished copying, and that the two files ending -wal and -shm
were copied with it.
ios.unreadable.title: The iPhone message store could not be read

search.index-unreadable.body:
The search index could not be used. It is a derived file and nothing in the
archive depends on it, so the fix is to build it again:

  amberkeep search --db msgstore.db --rebuild "your search"

If that keeps happening, check there is room on the disk: an index is
roughly a third the size of the archive.
search.index-unreadable.title: The search index could not be used

search.no-full-text-support.body:
This build cannot search, which should not be possible in a release and is
worth reporting.

Everything else still works: the archive can be exported and read as web
pages, which carry their own search.
search.no-full-text-support.title: This build cannot search

search.nothing-to-search-for.body:
There are no words in that search.

Type what you remember of the message. A part of a word works too, with a
star at the end: vermu* finds vermut and vermuts.
search.nothing-to-search-for.title: There are no words in that search

source.no-files-there.body:
That folder does not hold the phone's files.

What is wanted is the WhatsApp folder itself — on the phone it is
Android/media/com.whatsapp/WhatsApp — or the Media folder inside it. If you
can see a folder called Media when you open the one you named, name the one
above instead.

The archive opens without it, and shows the small copies WhatsApp keeps inside
the database.
source.no-files-there.title: There are no WhatsApp files in that folder

source.unrecognised-archive.body:
This is a database, but not one this version recognises.

Two files can be opened here: an Android msgstore.db, after decrypting, and
an iPhone ChatStorage.sqlite taken from a backup. The other databases that
sit beside them hold contacts and settings rather than messages.
source.unrecognised-archive.title: That database is not one this version recognises

sentences.a-day-ago: taken a day ago; anything said on the phone since is not in it
sentences.all-already-there: every message is already on the iPhone
sentences.cannot-see-safety: nothing here can see this; it is the only way back and it has to be done by hand
sentences.days-ago: taken {days} days ago; anything said on the phone since is not in it
sentences.has-room: There is room for a copy of the backup
sentences.hidden-identity: it has only a hidden identity, so it cannot be matched to a conversation on the iPhone
sentences.is-encrypted: it is encrypted, and an encrypted backup is sealed with a key that never leaves the phone
sentences.no-backup-files: it has none of the four files every Finder, iTunes and Apple Devices backup has
sentences.no-date: it does not say when it was taken
sentences.not-a-conversation: only conversations and groups can be moved
sentences.nothing-carries: nothing in it can be carried across
sentences.safety-backup: A safety backup exists and has been archived
sentences.thanks-ask: If this helped, you can buy me a coffee at {where}. It is voluntary, and nothing here depends on it.
sentences.warn-folded: {conversations} conversations turned out to be the same person the iPhone already has under another name, and will be written into the conversation that is already there rather than added beside it.
sentences.warn-folded-one: One conversation turned out to be the same person the iPhone already has under another name, and will be written into the conversation that is already there rather than added beside it.
sentences.warn-groups-left-out: {groups} groups were left out because groups were not included.
sentences.warn-groups-left-out-one: One group was left out because groups were not included.
sentences.warn-hidden-left-out: {conversations} conversations could not be matched to anyone, because WhatsApp hides some people behind an identifier this archive has no phone number for. They were left out rather than added as somebody new.
sentences.warn-hidden-left-out-one: One conversation could not be matched to anyone, because WhatsApp hides some people behind an identifier this archive has no phone number for. It was left out rather than added as somebody new.
sentences.warn-no-pairings: The iPhone files {conversations} conversations under a hidden identity rather than a phone number, and WhatsApp's own record of which is which was not supplied. Anybody in that position who is known by their number on the Android will arrive as a second conversation rather than joining the one already there. Supply LID.sqlite from the same backup to avoid it.
sentences.warn-no-pairings-one: The iPhone files one conversation under a hidden identity rather than a phone number, and WhatsApp's own record of which is which was not supplied. Anybody in that position who is known by their number on the Android will arrive as a second conversation rather than joining the one already there. Supply LID.sqlite from the same backup to avoid it.
sentences.warn-placeholders: {messages} messages will arrive as a line of text saying what was sent, not as the picture, recording or file itself. Those files are not in the backup this reads, and nothing here can invent them.
sentences.warn-placeholders-one: One message will arrive as a line of text saying what was sent, not as the picture, recording or file itself. That file is not in the backup this reads, and nothing here can invent it.
sentences.warn-untranslatable: {entries} entries will not come across at all: call history, and the notices WhatsApp writes into a conversation about itself. Nothing anybody typed is in that number.
sentences.warn-untranslatable-one: One entry will not come across at all: call history, or a notice WhatsApp wrote into a conversation about itself. Nothing anybody typed is in that number.

stages.restoring: Restoring, and what you will see

apps-and-passcode.body:
Apps are downloaded again from the App Store rather than restored, so the
phone needs the Apple ID password and Wi-Fi, and will look half-empty for a
while. The passcode is not set; set it again.

Saved passwords, Wi-Fi networks and Health data are not there, for the reason
given before any of this started.
apps-and-passcode.title: The phone will finish itself

check-it-worked.body:
Four things, in a minute:

  * The number of conversations looks right.
  * Open the oldest conversation you moved and look at its first message.
    The date should be the one the report said.
  * Names appear rather than phone numbers, in the conversations that had them.
  * Pictures that came across appear as a line of text saying what was sent.
    That is expected: the files themselves are not in the backup.

If any of those is wrong, do not take another backup. The archived one is
still the way back, and taking a backup now is the thing that would spoil it.
check-it-worked.title: Check it actually worked

decline-icloud.body:
When WhatsApp opens it may offer to restore your chat history from iCloud.

Decline it.

Accepting replaces the entire message history — including everything just
merged in — with whatever iCloud happens to hold. This is the single way to
undo the whole exercise in one tap, and it is offered as though it were
helpful.
decline-icloud.expect: WhatsApp opens on the conversation list with the merged history in it.
decline-icloud.title: Say no to restoring chats from iCloud

encryption-off.body:
In Finder, with the phone selected, untick "Encrypt local backup".

It will ask for the password you set a moment ago. This does not remove the
archived backup — that one stays encrypted and stays where it is.
encryption-off.expect: the tick disappears. Finder may start a new backup on its own; let it finish.
encryption-off.title: Turn off encrypted backups

error-211.body:
Find My iPhone was still on. Nothing was written to the phone and nothing has
been lost.

Turn it off and start the restore again.
error-211.title: If the restore stopped with error 211

find-my-back-on.body:
Settings, your name, Find My, Find My iPhone, on.

A phone without it is a phone that cannot be found or wiped if it is lost. It
was turned off for one hour and for one reason, and this is that reason ending.
find-my-back-on.title: Turn Find My iPhone back on

find-my-off.body:
On the phone: Settings, your name at the top, Find My, Find My iPhone, and
turn it off. It asks for the Apple ID password.

A restore with Find My still on stops at the very end with "error 211" and
nothing else. Nothing is written and nothing is lost, but it is an hour spent
for a number instead of a sentence.

Write down that you turned it off. It has to go back on afterwards, and by
then it is easy to forget it was ever off.
find-my-off.expect: the switch goes grey and the phone confirms it.
find-my-off.title: Turn off Find My iPhone

fresh-backup.body:
Back up to this Mac once more. This is the backup that will be changed and
restored, and it must be recent: anything said on the phone after this point
will not be in it and will be gone after the restore.

Say nothing on the phone from here until the restore has finished.
fresh-backup.expect: Finder shows a new date with no padlock beside it.
fresh-backup.title: Back the phone up again, unencrypted this time

go-back.body:
The archived encrypted backup from the first step is the way back, and it is
complete: everything as it was, Health data and passwords included.

In Finder, with the phone selected, choose Restore Backup and pick the
archived one. It will ask for the password set at the start.

Do this before taking any new backup. A new backup does not overwrite an
archived one, but it is not worth finding out otherwise while upset.
go-back.title: Going back

health-data-goes.body:
The backup this restores from has to be unencrypted, because an encrypted one
is sealed with a key that never leaves the phone and nothing on a computer can
open it.

An unencrypted backup does not contain Health data, saved passwords, Wi-Fi
networks, or the keychain. Restoring one means losing those, and there is no
way around it: it is Apple's design, not a limitation of this program.

If Health data matters more than the message history, stop here. The archived
encrypted backup from the previous step still has everything, and restoring
that puts the phone back exactly as it is now.
health-data-goes.expect: nothing yet. This is a decision, not an action.
health-data-goes.title: Know what an unencrypted backup does not carry

looks-stalled.body:
Partway through, the phone shows the Apple logo with a progress bar that does
not move for a long time. This is normal and it is the longest part.

Do not unplug it. Do not hold the power button. A phone interrupted here is a
phone that has to be restored again from the beginning.
looks-stalled.expect:
the bar eventually moves, the phone restarts a second time, and Setup
Assistant appears asking about language and Wi-Fi.
looks-stalled.title: The part that looks like it has frozen

power-and-space.body:
The phone on its cable and the computer on mains power. A restore that is
interrupted by a flat battery is the one way this goes badly wrong.

The computer needs free space for a second copy of the backup, which is as
large as the first.
power-and-space.title: Plug both in, and check there is room

reverify-number.body:
It sometimes asks to verify the number by text message. Keep the SIM in the
phone until this is done, or the message cannot arrive.

Verifying the number does not touch the messages already there.
reverify-number.title: WhatsApp may ask for the phone number again

safety-backup.body:
Connect the phone, open Finder, choose the phone in the sidebar, and back it
up to this Mac with "Encrypt local backup" switched ON. Set a password you
will not lose.

Then right-click that backup in Finder's list and choose Archive.

Archiving is the part people skip and the part that matters. Finder keeps one
backup per phone and writes over it the next time. Without archiving, the very
next backup — the one this process is about to make — replaces the only copy
of everything as it was. Archiving puts it somewhere Finder will leave alone.

Encrypted, because only an encrypted backup carries Health data, saved
passwords and Wi-Fi networks. This is the copy you would go back to.
safety-backup.expect:
the backup appears in Finder's list with a padlock and a date. Check the padlock
is there before going on: no padlock means it was not encrypted, and Health data
and passwords are not in it.
safety-backup.title: Make a safety backup, and archive it

start-restore.body:
In Finder, with the phone selected, choose Restore Backup and pick the one
this program made. Its date is today's.

Nothing you do on the computer from here will change the result. The phone is
being written to; leave it connected and leave it alone.
start-restore.expect: a progress bar on the computer first, then "Restore in progress" on the phone.
start-restore.title: Restore the changed backup

wrong-backup.body:
Finder lists backups by device and date. The changed one is a copy of the
original with today's date, in the same place Finder keeps the rest.

If it is not listed, Finder has not noticed it. Quit Finder and open it again
with the phone connected.
wrong-backup.title: If Finder will not show the changed backup
